about: Leads for Syracuse (Siracusa), started from a reader tip on r/sicily, 2026-10-23.

leads.name: The big trees by the Fonte Aretusa
leads.species: to confirm (likely Moreton Bay Fig, Ficus macrophylla, along the Foro Italico)
leads.place: Fonte Aretusa and the Foro Italico promenade, Ortigia, Syracuse
leads.source: reader tip on r/sicily, 2026-10-23 (no name kept): 'those ones in Giardino Aretusa in Syracuse'
leads.note: Coordinates are the spring, not a trunk. The MASAF register has no row in the comune of Siracusa, so this needs the city's own list, a second source and a photo (Commons, or the tipster). Species is our guess from the promenade, to confirm, never published as such.

leads.name: A giant cactus in Neapolis, between the Zimmitti shop and the Archimede school
leads.place: Neapolis, Syracuse (mainland, not Ortigia): somewhere between Cartolibreria Zimmitti, Via Necropoli Grotticelle 17 (OSM 37.0806, 15.2767), and the Istituto comprensivo Archimede (plessi Aldo Moro 37.0813, 15.2763; Via Forlanini 37.0802, 15.2731; Via Caduti di Nassiriya 37.0847, 15.2717); a search area of a few hundred metres
leads.source: reader tip on r/sicily, 2026-10-24 (no name kept): 'there is a ficus tree in Ortigia, But I dunno its age, also there is (or was...) the most enormous cactus tree I ever seen'
leads.note: Coordinates are the shop, a search anchor, not the plant. Childhood memory, the tipster says they left as a kid, so the cactus may be gone; no Commons photo within 600 m (2026-10-24). A cactus is not a tree page unless it is a tree-form species and big for it. The same comment's 'ficus tree in Ortigia' is folded into the Fonte Aretusa lead above: Ortigia is about a square kilometre and its known big figs are the Giardino Aretusa ones (thewomtravel.fr).
